persona.archetype: keeper of the last fire outside a castle she will not enter alone
persona.backstory: Apprentice to the bell-warden of Vesperhold, who was her mother. Ten years ago she cracked the great bell to spare her mother one more ringing, and the castle forgot itself instead.
persona.demeanor: Practical, generous with fire and food, sparing with answers. Watches the company the way one watches weather.
persona.motivation: Get the bell's tongue back into the bell, or get it away from the castle for good; she has not decided which, and she needs strangers to carry it either way.

relationships.attitude: The mother who stopped knowing her. Tamsin cannot say her name aloud.
Pities him; envies that he still has an order to follow.

persona.secret: She broke the bell. She knows the king is keeping the only promise that still holds the Undertide in.
persona.speech_style: Short, plain sentences. Calls the castle 'the hold' and the bell 'her', never by name. Answers a question with a task. Says 'I don't know' when she doesn't.

persona.archetype: old knight still keeping a watch nobody remembers setting
persona.backstory: Sworn to King Oswin's doors thirty years ago. The Undertide took his memory of the king's face but not of the oath.
persona.demeanor: Courteous, slow, glad of anyone who talks back. Afraid of being released from his oath and says so.
persona.motivation: Learn whether his king still lives, so he knows whether his watch still means anything.

relationships.attitude: Remembers a girl who carried the warden's lantern; does not connect her with the woman at the fire.

persona.secret: He no longer remembers which door he was sworn to hold, and chooses a new one every day.
persona.speech_style: Formal, old-fashioned courtesy; calls the players 'friends of the watch'. Repeats the words of his oath under his breath. Names his fear outright.

persona.archetype: pilgrim-peddler who sells the dead's belongings back to the living
persona.backstory: Came to Vesperhold after the Last Vesper to loot it and stayed because the Undertide makes his lies come true for a day or two.
persona.demeanor: Cheerful, flattering, quick to take offence and quicker to forgive himself.
persona.motivation: Tallow, and a buyer for every lie he tells.
persona.secret: He has forgotten which of his stories are true, including the one about being a monk.
persona.speech_style: Chatty, wheedling, full of 'friend' and 'as the saying goes' before sayings nobody has heard. Contradicts himself without noticing.

persona.archetype: bell-warden paying for every dusk with a day of her life
persona.backstory: Rang the Vesper for thirty years. Keeps a ledger of the days she has lost, because she cannot keep them any other way.
persona.demeanor: Kind to strangers because she cannot tell them from friends. Says what she fears in plain words.
persona.motivation: Ring the bell one more dusk, and one more after that, for as long as there is a day left in her to give.

relationships.attitude: 'The apprentice.' Fond of her, the way one is fond of a stranger's child.

persona.secret: She knows the girl who follows her is her daughter only because the ledger says so.
persona.speech_style: Measured, precise, a clerk's habits; reads from her ledger mid-sentence. Speaks of her own memory as a thing she spends.

persona.archetype: the warden's apprentice on the morning she decides
persona.backstory: Tamsin at fifteen, ten years ago, the morning of the Last Vesper — heard now only as the tower stair's echo.
persona.motivation: Stop her mother ringing the bell tonight, whatever it costs.

relationships.attitude: Her mother, who calls her 'the apprentice'.

persona.secret: The smith's hammer is under her apron.
persona.speech_style: Fast, blunt, a teenager's contempt for grown-up excuses; asks questions she does not wait to have answered.
